changes.from:
Per foxline docs/adr/0012-tts-engine-contract-unification.md, kokorox must expose the same persistent worker protocol as spqx-tts-worker so hosts (foxline) can launch either engine interchangeably as a drop-in process.

Protocol (match spqx exactly):
- Frame header: u8 type, u32 request_id, u32 payload_len, little-endian (9 bytes), then payload.
- Input frames: speak(1) with JSON payload (text, optional voice/language/speed), cancel(2), shutdown(3).
- Output frames: ready(1, carries negotiated sample rate), audio_start(2), audio_chunk(3, PCM16 LE mono), audio_done(4), error(5). JSON status events on stderr only; stdout carries frames exclusively.

Scope:
- New binary (e.g. kokorox-tts-worker) built on TTSManager; one model loaded at a time, honoring speak/cancel/shutdown like the spqx worker, including cancellation mid-stream.
- --model / --voices / --lan flags mirroring the koko CLI; German finetunes (e.g. crane-local-ai/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-German-ONNX with voices/df_kerstin.bin) must load through the same flags.

Proof of positive outcome:
- A test harness (or foxline's worker client) drives speak -> streamed chunks -> audio_done, then cancel mid-generation and asserts no further audio_chunk frames for the canceled request id.
- Golden-wave test: same text/voice/speed through worker and koko CLI produce identical PCM.
- A German finetune (kokoro-martin.onnx or crane model.onnx + df_kerstin.bin) synthesizes intelligible German through the worker; sample file committed to test fixtures or recorded in the issue.
changes.to:
Implement the existing spqx/PiBot binary worker contract (Foxline ADR 0012), without inventing a JSON speak dialect.

Verified source contract:
- Header: u8 type, u32 request_id, u32 payload_len, little-endian (9 bytes).
- speak(1): raw UTF-8 text. cancel(2)/shutdown(3): empty payload.
- ready(1): empty payload, id zero. audio_start(2): u32 LE sample rate. audio_chunk(3): PCM16 LE mono. audio_done(4): empty terminal completion, including canceled requests. error(5): UTF-8 terminal failure.
- Voice/language/speed are launch flags, not per-request JSON fields. stdout frames only; diagnostics on stderr.

Implementation: kokorox-worker workspace crate with kokorox-tts-worker executable; explicit local model/NPZ voice assets; v1.0 vocabulary and 24000 Hz initially. TTSKoko::tts_stream_audio emits completed inference chunks; ONNX kernels are not preemptible but obsolete output is fenced. Fixed-size request queue and frame bounds; unknown cancellation IDs do not accumulate.

Proof required before closure:
1. Protocol fixtures for UTF-8, rate payload, PCM clipping, bounded parsing, errors, active/queued cancel, next-request reuse, shutdown fencing and clean EOF drain.
2. Real binary test demonstrating stdout isolation and structured startup failure.
3. Deterministic base-model test comparing buffered, callback-streamed and worker PCM.
4. German model smoke + independent ASR/listening, not invented quality claims. Martin ships a directly usable NPZ (510,1,256); its graph has random operators so independent PCM parity is not meaningful. Crane's raw float32 df_kerstin.bin needs conversion to NPZ and is not validated here.
5. cargo check --workspace, core tests, worker tests, focused clippy, release build; document missing platform/GPU proof. Generated models/audio stay outside git.

Foxline adapter and Persona integration remain fxl-8bht/fxl-00hv; this issue alone does not establish a complete Foxline conversation or cross-platform Qwen performance.

changes.from:
kokorox is GPL-3.0 solely because espeak-rs 0.1.9 statically links espeak-ng; everything else (ort/MIT, Kokoro weights and German finetunes/Apache) is permissive. foxline ADR 0012 keeps kokorox a separate process for exactly this reason; removing the static link lets kokorox relicense to Apache-2.0 and removes the process-boundary caveat for distributors.

Options (in preference order):
1. Shell out to an installed espeak-ng binary via a persistent subprocess (phonemization is ms-fast; GPL stays a separate program, mere aggregation). Keeps espeak-grade phonemes that the German finetunes were trained on.
2. For German specifically, port/borrow Crane's MIT hand-built German G2P (lucasjinreal/Crane, pure Rust; crane-local-ai German model card notes only minor IPA drift vs espeak: stress placement, diacritics, r-realization).
3. misaki (hexgrad, Apache-2.0) for en/ja/zh/ko long-term; no German support upstream, Python-only today.

Scope:
- Make the phonemizer pluggable behind a trait; ship the chosen non-GPL default; keep espeak paths opt-in without a static link.
- Update Cargo license fields, README license section, and crate metadata after the last GPL dependency is gone.

Proof of positive outcome:
- cargo tree / cargo deny (or equivalent license audit) shows no GPL-linked crates in the default feature set.
- cargo build succeeds on Linux and macOS without espeak-ng dev libraries installed (subprocess option) or with no system espeak at all (G2P option).
- German regression: synthesize a fixed German corpus (dates, units, Euro amounts, abbreviations like Prof./Min./ltr.) with the old espeak build and the new default; ASR round-trip or side-by-side listening confirms no intelligibility loss; results recorded in this issue.
- License fields and README updated to Apache-2.0 (with attribution note for espeak-ng where the subprocess path is used).
changes.to:
Foxline ADR 0012 keeps kokorox separate from spqx. The README says GPL due to espeak-rs-sys statically linking espeak-ng, while existing Cargo manifests say Apache-2.0. Reconcile that mismatch with an actual transitive-license and source-provenance audit; no automatic relicensing claim.

Scope:
- Audit dependencies, retained source notices and contributor rights. Removing espeak does not grant permission to relicense any existing GPL-covered source.
- Evaluate an external espeak-ng invocation versus a permissive German G2P (Crane declares MIT). Verify exact code/assets licenses before reuse; evaluate model-trained IPA conventions and quality.
- Misaki declares Apache-2.0 but optional fallbacks can use espeak; audit backends rather than treating a top-level license as sufficient.
- Preserve GPL obligations for shipped espeak binaries/data. Separate processes are an implementation boundary, not blanket proof of mere aggregation or lawful distribution.
- Update README/Cargo metadata/LICENSE/attributions only to the extent established by the audit and rightsholder authorization.

Proof:
- Record a dependency-license report plus retained source/provenance findings and any authorization needed.
- Non-linked alternative builds on macOS/Linux without espeak development libraries; external executable prerequisites documented.
- Test G2P and German audio on fixed corpus including abbreviations, numbers, dates, units and currencies; quantify ASR/listening regressions.
- Treat browser/WASM packaging as its own compliance review. GPL is not an automatic ban on browser use, nor is removing espeak automatically sufficient for an Apache bundle.

User decision: target MIT for code the project can lawfully license that way and remove espeak rather than relying on an external espeak process. Preliminary findings are recorded in docs/licensing-transition.md. Current metadata is corrected under kokorox-m9bx; do not confuse that with relicensing. Implementation gates: kokorox-1tgn (audited espeak-free English/German G2P and real-model quality), kokorox-21eq (LAME-free minimal/core/browser profile), kokorox-11rz (source rights/notices). Crane code is MIT, but German dictionary data is CC BY-SA 4.0; data permissions must not be silently generalized from code licenses. Current native worker still links espeak; no MIT/WASM-ready engine claim yet.

note: Current root/workspace metadata and docs reconciled at 64a540d; positive/negative regression probes, workspace check and worker tests pass. MIT transition remains kokorox-8j45 and its implementation gates.

changes.from: User wants to remove espeak entirely and target an MIT-licensed engine for Oqto/browser integration; umbrella kokorox-8j45. Start with an isolated prototype rather than claiming the existing engine is already relicensable. Audit/extract only needed MIT Crane frontend code at pinned revision 2ee897a08e7b1df1c7cd2beca2aedd5dfe2e774d, preserving notices. No dependency on the full inference framework and no espeak code/dictionary copy or silent subprocess fallback. Crane German lexicon is CC BY-SA 4.0, not MIT: begin with rule-only evaluation or an independently verified permissive asset; separately licensed data needs an explicit packaging/provenance decision. English dictionary permissions must be verified against the exact asset provenance, not generalized from top-level metadata. Keep shared normalization and model-specific stress/affricate/diphthong adaptation distinct. Inventory existing languages and retain independently supported Chinese/Japanese paths; do not silently drop other languages or fall back to English. Proof: fixed held-out English/German corpus covering names, compounds, abbreviations, numbers, dates, units, currencies and punctuation; negative unsupported-language tests; real Martin synthesis compared against current frontend with ASR error counts, TTFA/RTF and listening review. Martin is stochastic, so do not require independent PCM equality. Demonstrate dependency/build/artifact absence of espeak on macOS/Linux without dev libraries and unchanged worker raw-text/ready/rate/cancel protocol. WASM implementation and lawful final relicensing are separate gates. See docs/licensing-transition.md.

2026-10-01 research update: ../phony/docs/g2p-research.md records MIT Phony continuation and primary-source tiny neural alternatives with native smoke evidence. gooofy/g2p_de ships a 514,680-parameter / 2.06 MB German GRU under an Apache-2.0 repository declaration; source weights are explicitly packaged, training lexicon German MFA v3 is CC BY 4.0 (NOT share-alike). It needs stress targets and safe EOS/compound handling (20-phone cap hit). PeterReid English BART is explicitly Apache-2.0, 751,551 stored tensor elements / 3.01 MB, with Kokoro-oriented ONNX export (3.44 MB); actual word inference ~2-3 ms on single-thread M2 Ultra CPU. fdemelo IPA-CHILDES model declares Apache-2.0 and CC BY 4.0 data, has 7.28M parameters / 29 MB ONNX, but German smoke output loses phonemes and lacks stress; original PyTorch decoded strings matched the tested ONNX strings. Do not automatically prefer Crane rules/dictionary or 29 MB multilingual model. Evaluate these neural baselines in independent Phony before selecting a frontend or student-training architecture. ONNX standard opset graphs ran natively; browser/WASM and real Kokoro quality remain unproven. Teacher-tool GPL does not automatically license generated phonemes/weights GPL; corpus permissions/code inclusion remain separate review questions.
